subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should OpenClaw treat cron runs that start but do not record success or error before timeout/restart as failed from a durable or external lifecycle path, and how should that alert be delivered when the Gateway event loop is unhealthy?
rationale: Source shows current failureAlert delivery is in-process and current startup recovery is after-the-fact; automation cannot choose whether to add an external watchdog, restart reconciliation semantics, or keep the existing in-process policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Durable Cron Failure Reporting
options.body: Record started/success/error transitions durably and surface stuck or interrupted runs after timeout/restart through a path that does not require the original wedged event loop.

options.title: Keep Alerts In Process
options.body: Treat current startup recovery and failureAlert behavior as sufficient, and close this issue only after macOS soak proof shows the Gateway no longer reaches the starvation state.

options.title: Fold Into Broad Memory Tracker
options.body: Move the remaining cron-reporting evidence into #54155 or #91588 and keep this issue only as historical context after maintainers confirm the scope boundary.

recommendation.title: Add Durable Cron Failure Reporting
recommendation.body: Record started/success/error transitions durably and surface stuck or interrupted runs after timeout/restart through a path that does not require the original wedged event loop.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed the memory watcher mitigation and set the broader Gateway RSS profiling closure bar, making them the strongest routing owner for the memory-versus-alerting boundary.
